name: Auren Baobab-Lychee Still
description: A lightly sparkling — almost still — street-brand soft drink from the Auren Collective, a worker-owned bottling operation in the Midden. Uses real baobab powder and synth-lychee in a low-sugar format with an almost wine-like body.
flavor_profile: Earthy, faintly tangy baobab with floral synth-lychee sweetness; very low carbonation gives it a smooth, almost syrupy mouthfeel; subtle fermented note on the finish that some find appealing and others find off-putting
cultural_context: The Auren Collective is a point of local pride in the Midden District — buying Auren products is a political statement as much as a preference; the brand has been the subject of two attempted buyouts by Selvane Beverage Co., both publicly refused.
story_hooks: The Auren Collective's real baobab supplier has suddenly tripled their price — someone is buying up baobab stocks across the corridor, and the Collective is three weeks from having to go full-synth.

An Auren bottle was found at a crime scene in Tier 4 territory — the victim, a corporate fixer, had no known connection to the Midden, and the bottle's batch code traces to a run that was never distributed.
A former Auren Collective member is trying to sell the original formula to Selvane — the Collective will stop them by any means necessary.
